tasks.short: Answer routine inquiries and refer patrons

steps.what: Answer routine inquiries from patrons at the desk
Show a stored answer for that routine inquiry
Refer patrons who need professional assistance to librarians

tasks.design: The assistant answers routine inquiries and refers patrons who need a librarian. {DOCS} shows a stored answer when the question identifier matches. An unknown question stays blank, and the assistant refers it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routine answers lived in memory, so every question took a search or a referral.
tasks.enabler_now: A known question identifier can open a short stored answer.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing the question, and judging that a librarian is needed, stay with the assistant.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant hears that the stored line does not fit and walks the patron to a librarian.
tasks.altitude: The assistant still owns the referral. A known question can be answered from the stored line.

reach.learn: Which routine questions the librarian wants sent across.

evidence.claim: A stored question identifier can show a routine answer. The referral to a librarian stays with the assistant.

assumptions: The work starts with a patron question and ends with an answer or a referral to a librarian.
An answer row has question identifier and answer text, written by a librarian. A missing row is left blank.
The referral is spoken or walked across. No machine sends it.
unknowns: Which questions the librarians are willing to store as routine.
research_questions: How many inquiries matched a stored answer, and how many were referred?

already_counted.description: Answering routine inquiries at the desk is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Tell a librarian when a stored answer no longer matches the question patrons ask.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few inquiries match a stored line, so the desk conversation remains. High: known inquiries show an answer, and referrals still go to a librarian. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Manage reserve materials by placing items for library patrons
Checking items in and out of the library
List reserve items past the stored removal date
Removing out-of-date reserve materials from the shelf

tasks.design: The assistant places reserve items, checks them in and out, and removes out-of-date ones. {DOCS} lists reserve rows whose removal date is already stored and earlier than today. A blank date stays off the list, and the assistant decides.
tasks.previous_blocker: The reserve shelf was checked by reading every card.
tasks.enabler_now: The removal date is a field, so the dated list is a comparison, not a judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Placing the item, the desk check, and taking it off the shelf stay physical.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant keeps an item a patron is standing there to collect, even if the date has passed.
tasks.altitude: The assistant still runs the reserve shelf. The dated list shows what is due off it.

reach.task: Decide how long a course reserve stays up
reach.learn: Which date the librarian set for that list.

evidence.claim: A stored removal date can list out-of-date reserve rows. Placing, checking, and removing items stay manual.

assumptions: The work starts with a reserve request or a return and ends when the item is placed, checked, or removed.
A reserve row has item identifier, patron identifier, and removal date, entered by the assistant at placing. A blank date is left blank.
Checking an item in or out at the desk is not replaced by the list.
unknowns: Who sets the removal date for a course reserve.
research_questions: How many out-of-date rows did the assistant still leave on the shelf, and why?

already_counted.description: Checking items in and out at the library desk is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct a removal date the assistant finds wrong while placing an item.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: removal dates are often blank, so the assistant still reads the shelf. High: dates are filled, and placing, checking, and removing remain. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lend materials and process inter-library loans

steps.what: Lend books, periodicals, and videotapes at circulation desks
Collect other materials at the circulation desks
Reserve books and other materials when a patron asks
Draft inter-library loans from the stored request
Process the inter-library loans after review of the request
Send the approved inter-library loan request

tasks.design: The assistant lends and collects books, periodicals, videotapes, and other materials at the circulation desk, and reserves items patrons ask for. {DOCS} drafts an inter-library loan from a stored patron and title. The assistant reviews that request, and {EMAIL} sends only the accepted version. A missing title or holding library stays blank and nothing is sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each loan request was retyped into a message, and the desk work was mixed in with it.
tasks.enabler_now: Patron and title identifiers are already on the request, so the message can be filled and stopped when one is missing.
tasks.still_hard: Handing the item across the desk, and judging an odd loan, stay with the assistant.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant refuses a loan the holding library should not release.
tasks.altitude: Desk lending stays the week. An inter-library request goes out only in the version the assistant accepted.

reach.task: Approve a loan the holding library disputes
reach.learn: Which titles are not lent outside.

evidence.claim: A stored patron and title can fill a loan request, and a missing identifier stops the send.
A loan request names a patron. The assistant accepts that text before it is sent. The design does not score patrons.

assumptions: The work starts at the circulation desk and ends with a loan, a return, a reserve, or a sent inter-library request.
A request row has patron identifier, title identifier, and holding library, entered by the assistant. A blank identifier is not invented.
The send uses the request version accepted in the review. A later change voids it. Desk lending is not a send.
unknowns: Which holding libraries accept a structured request.
research_questions: How many inter-library drafts stopped on a blank title, and how many were sent?

already_counted.description: Lending books and other materials at the circulation desk is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct a holding library on a request the assistant has not yet accepted.

approvals.approved_version: inter-library loan request the assistant accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most loans are walk-up, and inter-library details are rarely complete. High: complete requests are sent after review, and the desk loan still takes the time. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct patrons on catalogues and systems

steps.what: Instruct patrons on reference sources and card catalogs
Instruct patrons on automated information systems
Open the stored guide for that catalog system

tasks.design: The assistant instructs patrons on reference sources, card catalogs, and automated information systems. {DOCS} opens the short guide when the system identifier is stored. A missing guide stays blank, and the assistant demonstrates.
tasks.previous_blocker: The assistant remembered the clicks, and each patron started from nothing.
tasks.enabler_now: A known system name can open the same short guide.
tasks.still_hard: Standing with the patron and seeing where they are stuck stay manual.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant changes the explanation when the patron cannot use the screen.
tasks.altitude: Instruction stays the work. The guide is only a page to point at.

reach.task: Rewrite a guide for a reference source
reach.learn: Which sources the librarian still wants taught by hand.

evidence.claim: A stored system identifier can open a short guide. Instructing the patron stays manual.

assumptions: The work starts when a patron asks how to search and ends when they can take the next step or the assistant stops.
A guide row has system identifier and steps, written by a librarian. A missing guide is left blank.
Upkeep is zero beyond fixing a guide line the librarian has already rewritten. The hour covers that correction.
unknowns: Which systems patrons still need shown in person.
research_questions: How often was the guide opened, and how often did the assistant ignore it?

already_counted.description: Instructing patrons on reference sources and catalogs is already in the assistant's step.

incremental.description: Correct a guide line after a librarian rewrites that source.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: patrons need a demonstration, so the guide is rarely enough. High: known systems open a guide, and the assistant still instructs. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The assistant still meets patrons, shelves items, and handles cash. A record, notice, invoice, or order is written or sent only after the assistant accepts that version.
reach: A librarian receives the question the assistant could not answer from the desk.
A finance colleague receives only an invoice the assistant has accepted.
skills_to_grow: Stop when a required field is blank.
Accept or refuse the exact version before a send or a write.
Keep shelving, cash, and patron conversations in their own hands.
role.ambitious_version: Every item on loan has a location and a due date the desk can trust, and the assistant still decides the exception.
